about: Ideas tested in the projection lab. Numbers are from lab/replay.py on the 2025-26 season (with 2024-25 as the 'last season' prior) and checked on 2024-25. 'Accuracy' is the Brier score of SWISH's own chances on pretend lines (lower = better); minutes and points misses are average absolute errors. Each comparison uses the same player-nights for both versions.

experiments.idea: Share a newly-out player's minutes (his share of a 240-minute game)
experiments.why: Murray was ruled out on 29 Oct and SWISH barely moved his teammates' minutes.
experiments.scope: 4,199 player-nights where it changed minutes by 1+ (2025-26)
experiments.note: It handed out about 2 minutes too many to each teammate it touched.

experiments.idea: Bench player listed to start → full starter minutes
experiments.why: Herbert Jones started for Murray and played 32 minutes.
experiments.note: Right direction, far too strong: it overshot by about 2.6 minutes.

experiments.idea: Bench player listed to start → a third of the way to starter minutes
experiments.why: Softer version of the rule above.

experiments.idea: Trim big minutes: 10% of anything above 28 expected minutes
experiments.why: Players expected to play 32+ minutes averaged 1.1–1.5 minutes fewer (rest, blowouts, fouls).
experiments.note: Half of the old '1.2 minutes too many' was players who didn't play at all — those bets are void at the bookmaker, so it never cost money.

experiments.why: When SWISH said 60–65% on live picks it happened 50%; in the lab 68% happened 61%.
experiments.note: Combined with the minutes trim: accuracy 0.24282 → 0.24215 (2025-26) and 0.24401 → 0.24348 (2024-25). Fewer props reach 'strong' — that's intended.
Too wide: accuracy got worse again. 15% was the sweet spot.

experiments.idea: With vs without: a teammate's minutes in past games without the absent player
experiments.why: To decide from real games, not a rule, who takes a newly-out player's minutes.
experiments.scope: 5,498 player-nights where it moved minutes by 1+ (2025-26); both seasons overall
experiments.note: Tried 9 versions (stronger caution, more games needed, replacing or adding to the current rule): every one was worse on both seasons. Past 'without' games are too few and too mixed up with other absences and blowouts to trust. Confirmed starting lineups remain the best signal.

experiments.idea: Let the 240-minute gap work when stars are out: ignore fringe players' minutes (fewer than 3 games this season, or weighted by how often they've played lately)
experiments.why: 30 Oct: Sengun and J. Brown out, but players with 1–2 games carried last season's minutes, so nobody got more minutes (Capela played 30, expected 17).
experiments.scope: Players on teams with a 10+ minute player out, both seasons (≈400–4,300 player-nights per version)
experiments.note: Tried 6 versions (only 3+ game players count, weight by recent appearances, same-position players only, half the gap): every one gave minutes to players who then played LESS than expected (by 1.8–2.5 min). Freed minutes mostly go to deep-bench and garbage-time players who don't have props. 30 Oct was a real miss, but the current rule is right on average.

experiments.idea: Treat an absence as 'new' for 2 or 3 games (keeps 'lineup due' on hold longer)
experiments.why: Sengun had already missed 29 Oct, so on 30 Oct his teammates weren't put on hold.
experiments.scope: Extra props that would be held (420–800 per season, no lineups known)
experiments.note: 'Before' = props not held, 'after' = the extra props that would be held. 2025-26: they were no harder to predict than normal. 2024-25: a bit harder. Not clear enough to hold more picks — kept at 1 game.

experiments.idea: Back from an absence: a player who missed his team's last game gets 7.5% fewer expected minutes
experiments.why: 30 Oct: Tre Johnson (back from Achilles) was a strong over at 23 minutes and played 13.
experiments.scope: Players who missed their team's last game, both seasons (≈1,760–1,920 player-nights per run)
experiments.note: These players were projected 1.7–2.1 minutes too high and their overs hit only 37–45%. 5% and 10% also helped; 15% overshot. Plus an 'On hold · back from injury' label on OVERS when he is also on today's injury report (can't be tested in the lab — the report isn't in old box scores). Saved picks 28–30 Oct: strong 7–8 → 7–7 (Tre Johnson no longer strong).

experiments.idea: Confidence stretch: SWISH's own chance pulled toward 50% (sigmoid(0.70 × logit p)) before the 30/70 market blend
experiments.why: Lab 30 Oct: SWISH's own chances were overconfident on every market (e.g. PTS says 59% → happens 52%).
experiments.scope: Every player/market, both seasons (≈61k + 54k projections), lineups on; 2025-26 also without lineups
experiments.note: Projections unchanged; only chances move. Better in all 9 market/season/lineup runs. Very confident chances (70%+): 2025-26 said 76% won 69% → now said 75% won 75%; ~70% fewer of them. 0.70 was fitted on one season and tested on the other (30 Oct).

experiments.idea: Blowout minutes: when ESPN's spread is over 9, players expected 24+ min lose 0.25 min per point over 9 per 10 min above 24 (BLOWOUT_FROM 9, BLOWOUT_A 0.25)
experiments.why: 2025-26: players expected 30+ min in games with spread 11+ played 1.5–1.9 min less than projected.
experiments.scope: 2025-26 (only season with ESPN lines: 980/1,235 games); tuned Oct–Jan, checked Feb–Apr
experiments.note: Big-minute players in 11+ spread games: minutes miss 4.45→4.42 (tune), 4.98→4.75 (check), bias −2.0→−0.9. Stronger settings overshoot. Bench gain version made things worse. 'Shrink minutes toward the middle' (from the 4 live nights) was NOT supported over a full season.

experiments.idea: Team implied points (from ESPN total and spread) scale REB and AST: × (implied/115)^0.5. Points left alone.
experiments.why: 2025-26: per-minute REB/AST ran 3–7% higher than projected in high-scoring games, lower in low ones.
experiments.scope: 2025-26, tuned Oct–Jan (strength 0.25–2.0 tried), checked Feb–Apr; lineups on and off
experiments.note: Numbers are both changes together. PTS got worse with any total strength ≥0.5 (scoring rates already carry team pace). Saved real picks (1,043, real prices, lab/backtest_saved.py): Brier vs market unchanged (+0.0035 → +0.0036), strong 2–2 → 3–2, all −£153.58 → −£168.23 — no measurable gain against the bookies, as expected since they price totals and spreads already.

experiments.idea: Give teammates a share of a newly-out star's minutes even when the roster fills 240
experiments.scope: 2025-26 (11 versions, with and without lineups); best-balanced version shown (40% share)
experiments.note: Measured first: teammates of a newly-out 25+ min player really do play ~1 min more than projected (bench, same position most). The fixes removed that average shortfall but minutes error got worse in every version on both seasons: the extra minutes go to the wrong players. Same lesson as with-vs-without (30 Oct).
